evidence: dead_air: The hook (hook@1.5, hook@2.2) and seg0 (seg0:start to seg0:end, about 1.7s to 5.8s) are the same finished bar chart. Only the mascot's face changes. Code measured a 6.33s hold.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:start, seg3:mid and seg3:end show two identical circles. Both read '127%' and both are labelled 'Billionaire wealth', while the narration says the S&P 500 grew 195%. The disc carrying the S&P figure is a duplicate of the billionaire one, and the same wrong pair stays on screen through seg4 and the payoff.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The comparison composer bound the same series to both slots, so the second entry (S&P 500, 195%) was never used. It also draws the two values as pulsing discs, not as a comparison a viewer can see.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show billionaire wealth +127% against the S&P 500 +195% as two clearly different things, labelled 'Billionaire wealth' and 'S&P 500'. The S&P quantity should visibly overtake the billionaire one, for example two stacks of money growing side by side. Data should cause the growth, for example by feeding the S&P stack, so the 'it's just stocks' claim lands visually.
